title: Wedge-tailed eagle modelling
text: This site collects the analysis notebooks for modelling the flight behaviour of GPS-tracked wedge-tailed eagles (Aquila audax fleayi) in Tasmania.

title: Wedge-tailed eagle modelling
text:
Behaviour classification

K-means Instantaneous Variable: using variables calculated for each GPS fix to estimate behavioural states.
K-means Cumulative Variables: using variables that aggregate over a moving window (such as cumulative turning angles or average speed) to estimate behavioural states. This approach helps to smooth over jumpy states when using k-means, which treats each each sample independently.

title: Wedge-tailed eagle behavioural classification
text:
Choosing k
Next, we’ll do some plotting to help us choose K.

Within-sum-of-squares plot


Show code
wss_df = data.frame(k = 2:7, 
                    wss = c(k2$tot.withinss,
                            k3$tot.withinss,
                            k4$tot.withinss,
                            k5$tot.withinss,
                            k6$tot.withinss,
                            k7$tot.withinss))

#Looking for an elbow, in order to determine "best k":
with(wss_df, plot(k,wss,type='b'))









Show code
#no obvious elbow.  




Bootstrap the average silhouette width
Calculate the average silhouettes for B=100 bootstrap samples of size 1000 each (for computational ease). In paper, B = 1000 of size 10,000 each.


Show code
B <- 100
avg.sils <- matrix(NA,B,6)
set.seed(992021)
for(b in 1:B){
  ids <- sample(1:nrow(ready_to_cluster),1000,replace=TRUE) 
  distmat <- dist(ready_to_cluster[ids,])
  clusters <- list(k2$cluster[ids],
                   k3$cluster[ids],
                   k4$cluster[ids],
                   k5$cluster[ids],
                   k6$cluster[ids],
                   k7$cluster[ids])
  for(i in 1:6) {
    sil <- silhouette(clusters[[i]],distmat) 
    avg.sils[b,i] <- mean(sil[,3])
  }
}




Show code
plot(2:7, 
     avg.sils[1,],
     type='b',
     col='#00000040', 
     ylab='Average silhouette width', xlab = 'K',
     ylim=c(0.22,0.35)
     )

for(i in 2:nrow(avg.sils)) lines(2:7, avg.sils[i,],type='b',col='#00000040')

title: Wedge-tailed eagle behavioural classification
text:
Relationships of the flight variables

K = 3 clusters
Note that the cluster labels are different from those in the Bergen et al. (2022) paper, due to different starting points in the k-means as the data here is just a subset of the data in the paper.
Also, we have tried to remove perching fixes beforehand (but some still may remain). We will therefore identify the other three behaviours (ascending, flapping, gliding).


Show code
eagle_subset <- eagle_subset %>% 
  mutate(behavior = case_when(
                              k3==1~'gliding',
                              k3==2~'flapping',
                              k3==3~'ascending')
         ) %>% 
  mutate(behavior = factor(behavior, levels = c('gliding','ascending','flapping')))



Altitude above groundAbsolute turn angleSpeed over groundVertical rate


We remove outliers for clarity and faster plotting.


Show code
ggplot(data = eagle_subset) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = behavior, fill = behavior, y = F_AOG), outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) + 
  ylim(0, 1000) +
  labs(x = "Behavior", y = "Altitude above ground (m)") +
  theme_bw()













Show code
# it looks like Silas didn't actually use Radians. He used absolute turn angle (create this column and plot)
eagle_subset$abs_angle = abs(eagle_subset$step_ta)

ggplot(data = eagle_subset) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = behavior, fill = behavior, y = abs_angle), outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values =cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) +
  labs(x = "Behavior", y = "Absolute turn angle (radians)") +
  theme_bw()













Show code

  geom_boxplot(aes(x = behavior, fill = behavior, y = F_Sn), outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) + 
  ylim(0, 25) +
  labs(x = "Behavior", y = "Speed (m/s)") +
  theme_bw()













Show code

  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), linetype=2) +
  labs(x = "Behavior", y = "Vertical rate (m/s)") +
  theme_bw()

Through time plots (x-time)

AltitudeSpeedVertical rateTurning angles




Show code
# calculate the time in seconds from the first point in the segment
segment_to_plot$seconds = segment_to_plot$stepend_dtime - segment_to_plot[[1,6]]

ggplot(data = segment_to_plot,aes(x = seconds, y = F_AOG)) +
  geom_point(aes(col = as.factor(behavior)),size=.5) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
